public_rationale: The denial of substantive efficiency work conflicts with disclosures predating January 29, 2025. [e1, e2, e3, e4] On April 18, 2024, Meta described training infrastructure improvements and reported roughly threefold higher Llama 3 training efficiency than Llama 2. [e1] On May 14, 2024, Google described Gemini 1.5 Flash as a smaller model trained through distillation from 1.5 Pro. [e2] OpenAI's July 18, 2024 GPT-4o mini announcement documented an improved tokenizer shared with GPT-4o. [e3] Anthropic's March 4, 2024 disclosure described Claude 3 Haiku as its fastest, most compact model, with availability still forthcoming. [e4] These records establish efficiency engineering and model development, but do not settle how inefficient the models remained. [e1, e2, e3, e4]
limitations: The disclosures do not provide a common capability-adjusted resource comparison or settle the unmeasured description 'horribly inefficient.' [e1, e2, e3, e4]
Company-reported improvements do not independently establish optimal resource use or whether investment in efficiency was sufficient. [e1, e2, e3, e4]

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current models from Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic are horribly inefficient, and their makers never really tried to make them efficient.

statement.excerpt: The current models developed by both the hyperscalers (Gemini, Llama, et. al) and multi-billion-dollar "startups" like OpenAI and Anthropic are horribly inefficient, I had just made the mistake of assuming that they'd actually tried to make them more efficient.

from_speaker: assuming that they'd actually tried to make them more efficient
our_interpretation: Read the factual assertion as an absence of substantive efficiency work implemented in the models available by the post.
The broader post acknowledges efficiency teams and an earlier OpenAI attempt. Therefore, do not interpret this as a literal assertion that no employee ever researched efficiency.
Read efficiency ordinarily as reducing training or inference resources while preserving useful capability. Lower API prices alone do not establish lower production costs.
Use the latest model disclosures available by January 29, 2025. The retrospective assertion about development efforts has no stated starting date.
No numerical threshold is supplied for 'horribly'; the verdict tests the claimed lack of substantive effort, not optimality.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable measurements establish substantial avoidable resource use, and development records substantiate the claimed absence of meaningful efficiency efforts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Dated records show substantive efficiency engineering implemented before the post in the named model families.

evidence.locator: Training infrastructure discussion immediately before 'Instruction fine-tuning'
evidence.explanation: Meta describes concrete changes to parallelization, reliability, storage and training infrastructure, alongside inference optimizations. This is substantive efficiency engineering, although the improvement magnitude is company-reported.

evidence.locator: Section 'The new 1.5 Flash, optimized for speed and efficiency'
evidence.explanation: Google describes Gemini Flash as an efficiency-oriented model and explains its distillation from Pro. This documents an implemented effort before the post.

evidence.locator: Introduction, paragraph describing context length and tokenization
evidence.explanation: The announcement documents a concrete tokenizer improvement shared with GPT-4o, alongside the smaller model's release. This establishes engineering effort without treating API pricing as a measurement of underlying compute cost.

Anthropic describes an intentionally compact model within a family designed around capability, speed and cost tradeoffs. This documents efficiency-oriented model development, not proof of optimal resource use.
